name: sentry
description: Developer-first error tracking and performance monitoring
one_liner: A dashboard that tells a software team the moment their app breaks for a real user — what broke, which line of code, and how often — instead of waiting for a customer complaint.
buyer: An engineering manager at a company whose app has paying users and can't afford to fly blind when something crashes in production.
business_use_cases: A startup self-hosts it to avoid per-seat SaaS monitoring fees once their error volume grows past the free tier of hosted alternatives.
An agency building apps for clients bundles self-hosted error monitoring into its support retainer as a value-add.
A dev-tools consultant offers 'production health audits' using it to show a client where their app is silently failing.

money_ideas.idea: Offer managed self-hosting and setup as a service for companies that want Sentry's features without running the infrastructure themselves.
Bundle a one-time 'production health audit' using it to find and triage a client's hidden error backlog.

steal_this: This is a mature, already-commercialized project (Sentry the company); the realistic weekend move is reselling setup and triage services around the open-source self-hosted version, not competing with it directly.
